full_judgment:
Bimalendu Bikash Roy Chowdhury, J:- Plaintiff-respondent No.1, brought, Other Class Suit No. 44 of 1985 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Jamalpur for declaration of title and recovery of possession in respect of .46 acre of land comprised within Plot No. 6 measuring more or less 2.07 acres appertaining to C.S. Khatian No. 129 of mouza Bhabki and obtained a decree in his favour. The defendant-petitioners who contested the suit preferred Other Class Appeal No. 59 of 3991 to the District Judge, Jamalpur. The appellate court reversed the decision of the trial court and dismissed the suit on 28 February 1994. The plaintiff-respondent went up in revision, Civil Revision 1782 of 1994 to the High Court Division. A Single Bench of the said court, by judgment and order dated 12 November 1998, made the Rule absolute and restored the decree of the trial court after setting aside the dismissal by the appellate court. The defendants now seek leave to appeal there from. 

 2. Briefly stated the case of the plaintiff is as follows. The disputed holding originally belonged to Denatullah, Kefatullah, Zahir, Ismail and Jiar and their names were duly recorded in the C.S. Khatian. They sold their shares in the disputed plot to one Moniruddin Bepari by a registered kabala dated 19 December 1920. At the time of sale Zahir and Ismail were minors and so their mother Joynab Bewa executed the deed. After the death of Zahir and Ismail Kefatullah disputed the sale by Joynab on behalf of her minor sons. The two sons of Moniruddin namely, Naimuddin and Mafizuddin were obliged to purchase 44 acre of land from Kefatullah on 29 December 1949. Moniruddin died leaving behind 4 sons namely, Naimuddin, Mafizuddin, Kazimuddin and Ayenuddin. There was an amicable partition amongst the co-sharers and Naimuddin and Mafizuddin got the suit plot and had it recorded in the R O. R in their names. Mafizuddin died leaving two sons—Salu and Kalu and a daughter Kamala Khatoon. Kalu sold his share to Salu. Salu sold his share to Kazimuddin and Kafiluddin. Kamala sold her share to the defendants. Naimuddin transferred his molly share to the plaintiff by a deed of Heba on 20 February 1968. Thus the plaintiff came to possess 1.03 acre of land on the eastern side of the suit plot. He then sold out .57 acre of land out of his share to one Boyezuddin keeping the suit land in his possession. The defendants who are desperate people dispossessed the plaintiff from the suit land in the middle of January 1978. 

 8. It appears that both the trial court and the High Court Division on consideration of the evidence on record believed the case of the plaintiff as to his title and possession of the suit land and disbelieved the plea of the defendants that Genduli had ever got possession of any portion of the suit plot by amicable partition. Both the courts apparently depended largely on C.S. Khatian and the subsequent Khatian, besides want of any cogent proof in support of the defendants' plea. They also rightly considered Exhibit-1 whereby the entire plot was sold by the C.S. recorded owners. The appellate court missed these aspects of the case. The said court also did not advert to the findings of the trial court while reversing its judgment. We find nothing to disagree with the view of the High Court Division.
